The `collekt` command line is a thin wrapper around the same objects used by the
Python API: a region and time window, a `DatasetConfig` YAML selection, and a
runtime output directory.

## Fetch Data

Use `collekt fetch` to download source-native files for a request. A dataset
selection is required and the output directory is runtime state, not part of the
selection file.

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --bbox -6 20 35 45 \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --end 2023-06-15 \
  --dataset-config westmed.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections
```

`--bbox` uses `WEST EAST SOUTH NORTH` order. The same request can also use a
point radius:

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --at-lat 43.3 \
  --at-lon 5.4 \
  --radius 50 \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --dataset-config westmed.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections
```

or a GeoJSON region:

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --region regions/west-med.geojson \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --dataset-config westmed.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections
```

If `--end` is omitted, it defaults to the start day. If `--start` is omitted,
the request defaults to the current UTC day.

## Dataset Selection

`--dataset-config` points to a YAML version of `DatasetConfig`. It names the
desired datasets and provider parameters; the source catalog remains bundled with
the package, or supplied through `--conf-dir`.

```yaml
datasets:
  - provider: cmems
    key: cmems_glorys_my
    variables: [uo, vo]
    depth: [1.0, 1.1]
  - provider: cmems
    key: cmems_duacs_my
    variables: [ugos, vgos]
  - provider: skytruth
    key: skytruth
```

For CMEMS, select variables from the catalog's `available_variables`. Datasets
with depth require a `depth: [min, max]` range. See [Products](products.qmd) for
the bundled source keys and [Credentials](credentials.qmd) for provider secrets.

## Planning

Use `--dry-run` to inspect the planned provider requests without downloading
files.

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --bbox -6 20 35 45 \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --dataset-config westmed.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections \
  --dry-run
```

The dry-run table reports each source, requested day, availability status,
dataset ID, variables, and planned output path.

Add `--batch-days 7` to group retrieval work into at most seven UTC calendar
days. The default leaves source behavior unchanged. With batching enabled,
`--dry-run` also shows retrieval groups separately from output files; each group
may involve several provider requests. Daily sources retain daily output files.
See [Batch downloads](batching.qmd) for provider-specific behavior and limits.

## Cache and Strict Mode

By default, `fetch` reuses files already present under the output directory.
Pass `--no-cache` to force a new download.

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --bbox -6 20 35 45 \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --dataset-config westmed.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections \
  --no-cache
```

Pass `--strict` when skipped sources should make the command fail instead of
being reported in the result summary.

## Catalog Overlays

Use `--conf-dir` when a project needs to add or override source catalog entries.
The directory is merged on top of the bundled catalog.

```bash
collekt fetch \
  --bbox -6 20 35 45 \
  --start 2023-06-15 \
  --conf-dir my_brick/conf \
  --dataset-config presets/currents.yaml \
  --output-dir data/collections
```

The selection file still contains only the requested datasets. The catalog
overlay defines what datasets exist.

## Diagnostics

`collekt doctor` checks provider packages, credentials, catalog consistency, and
flags any source config key not recognized by its adapter (a likely typo, e.g.
`pad_dg` instead of `pad_deg`) as a warning.

```bash
collekt doctor
```

Pass `--online` to validate CMEMS datasets, variables, and declared coverage
against the Copernicus Marine catalogue.

```bash
collekt doctor --online
```

Use the same catalog overlay mechanism when checking downstream source entries.

```bash
collekt doctor --conf-dir my_brick/conf --online
```

The command exits with a non-zero status if any check fails.

## Inspect Configuration

`collekt config show` prints the merged configuration as YAML.

```bash
collekt config show
collekt config show --conf-dir my_brick/conf
```

Use it to verify that a catalog overlay is visible before running a fetch.
